advisories.message: Seven of the ten selected source rasters remain permission- or publisher-gated: five Julius O. Smith/PARSHL figures and two Oppenheim–Schafer quantization figures. The ledger and briefs preserve rights review or recomputation/rights-cleared-data fallbacks. ITU-T Q.23/Q.24 are freely readable and may be cited and paraphrased, but their prose, tables, and figures must not be republished or adapted without permission; the dossier and DTMF figure plan preserve that restriction.

verification.itu_q23_status_verified: Q.23 (11/1988) is listed in force and freely available by ITU-T.
verification.itu_q24_status_verified: Q.24 (11/1988) is listed in force and freely available by ITU-T.
verification.itu_clause_claims_verified: Q.23 §§6–7 support the frequency groups, allocation, ±1.8% transmit tolerance, and 20 dB distortion limit; Q.24 §§2.2–2.5 support exactly-one-per-group validity, tolerance, level/twist considerations, and timing categories; Annex A contains administration-specific example values.
verification.itu_rights_restriction_verified: The official PDFs state ITU copyright and require written permission for reproduction; the source registry, scope, read, summary, cache, sidecar, and brief avoid reproducing the protected table/figure and preserve the restriction.
mit6341_pointers_verified: Finite-word structures and sensitivity: Lecture 7 pp. 1–20 and PS4.
Multirate and polyphase: Lectures 10–11 and PS5–PS6.
STFT and modulated filter banks: Lecture 21 pp. 1–5, Lecture 22 pp. 1–6, and PS10.
FIR linear phase and dense-grid exchange verification: Lecture 2 pp. 5–6 and Lecture 9 pp. 4–6.
verification.oppenheim_pointer_verified: The researched second edition places rate conversion in chapter 4 §§4.6–4.9 and the decimation alias sum in §4.6.1; chapter 11 is Discrete Hilbert Transforms.
